title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or, becomes 1st player to claim two awards in one night
content: Harry Kane made history at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win football’s most prestigious individual honour. The Bayern Munich striker also claimed the Gerd Müller Trophy, completing a historic double after scoring 73 goals for club and country. His extraordinary campaign marks a defining moment in his career and English football history.

title: Microsoft extends buyouts to 60,000 staff in India, US, UK and Canada
content: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees in India, the US, the UK and Canada under a new Voluntary Exit Offer, announced in a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman. Open up to level 70, the offer has no age, tenure or performance criteria and mirrors standard severance. Employees have until early December to decide. The move follows 4,800 Microsoft layoffs in July.

title: Texas couple lose 70-acre family land after mother excludes son from her will
content: A Texas couple have lost their legal battle to remain on 70 acres of land they say had been in their family for decades. The dispute began after William Dan Moss was excluded from his mother's will. Despite challenging the inheritance decision and subsequent eviction, William and his wife, Brenda, failed to overturn the rulings. On October 22, a Texas appeals court upheld the eviction judgment.

title: Tyler Perry lists 22.5-acre mansion where Harry and Meghan stayed for $57m
content: Tyler Perry has listed his Beverly Hills mansion for $57 million amid plans to relocate to Puerto Rico. The estate, known for hosting Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, spans approximately 24,600 square feet. Featuring eight bedrooms and extensive amenities, it offers privacy within the exclusive Beverly Ridge Estates community. Perry developed the mansion over several years, completing it in 2012 after acquiring the land in 2004.

title: Lawmaker seeks nearly 200 withheld texts in fight over Trump's Kennedy Center
content: A Democratic US lawmaker has asked a federal judge to order the Trump administration to release nearly 200 withheld text messages concerning Washington's Kennedy Center. The request comes amid a legal dispute over plans to close the performing arts centre for renovations, months after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been illegally added to the building and ordered its removal.

title: Bill Gates says Meta’s Muse is the first great consumer AI product, but has one worry
content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has called Meta's Muse "the first truly great consumer AI product" in an interview with The Verge, revealing he congratulated chief AI officer Alexandr Wang on the personal AI agent. Gates said Muse stands out because it actually gets tasks done, but warned that open-weight AI models with removable safeguards are irresponsible, a week after Meta released its own Muse Spark Open.

title: US court says detained migrants have no constitutional right to bond hearings
content: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has made a pivotal ruling concerning immigrant detention, involving three men who unlawfully entered the country. The court decided to overturn earlier decisions that allowed them individualized bond hearings while awaiting removal proceedings. This change stirs substantial dialogue on the potential impacts on the constitutional rights of immigrants facing detention without due process.

title: The Rock’s $800M fortune: How Dwayne Johnson built his global empire
content: Dwayne Johnson has taken his wrestling fame and turned it into a global entertainment and business empire spanning Hollywood, production, consumer brands and real estate. Years of strategic career choices have taken him from WWE superstar to one of the world’s most recognizable entertainers. Johnson is married to Lauren Hashian, and he juggles family life with big projects outside the wrestling ring and movie sets.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million estate faces new setback as neighbors object
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

title: Saudi Arabia turns to AI system to hunt Houthi missiles; why it may not be effective
content: Saudi Arabia is utilizing artificial intelligence to improve its military response to Houthi missile operations. The US military’s Maven Smart System aids in detecting potential threats and identifying targets quickly. Despite its advantages, challenges remain due to the Houthis’ mobile tactics and rugged terrain. Concerns over civilian casualties and targeting errors further complicate the operation's effectiveness. Increased efficiency may not guarantee a decisive victory in this ongoing conflict.

title: Parliaments can serve as bridges to ease global tensions, says Birla
content:
File photo: Parliaments could be bridges of understanding, ease international tensions: Om Birla

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said on Monday that parliaments as expressions of the people’s will could serve as bridges to ease international tensions at a time of global uncertainty, heightened by regional conflicts, wars, terrorism and trade disruptions, and called on Brics legislatures to foster collective action. Inaugurating the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum, he said the consequences of geopolitical and economic headwinds transcended national boundaries and must be met with a spirit of collective responsibility. “These shared aspirations provided a strong foundation for deeper engagement and purposeful cooperation. The Brics Parliamentary Forum must therefore emerge as a dynamic platform for building confidence, fostering understanding and advancing collective action in pursuit of these common goals,” the LS Speaker added.

End of Article

content: the government is expected to announce changes to parcoursup . students have criticised its selection criteria, arguing that they lack transparency and limit equal access to preferred courses . the government will announce concrete measures after weeks of protests, school blockades and demonstrations continue to fuel unrest .

content: the existing platform, Parcoursup, will undergo “substantial change” for the 2027 admissions round before being replaced the following year . the government also promised smaller classes, additional teaching posts, more higher education places, increased student grants and funding for building renovations .
